title: Towards Natural Personalization: Evaluating Long-Horizon Preference Following in Personalized User-LLM Interactions
abstract: arXiv:2603.04191v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly serving as personal assistants, where users may share individual preferences over extended interactions. However, assessing how well LLMs can follow these preferences in natural, long-term situations remains underexplored. This work proposes RealPref, a benchmark for evaluating natural preference-following in personalized user-LLM interactions. RealPref features 100 synthetic user profiles, 1300 personalized preferences, 4 types of preference expression (from explicit to implicit), and long-horizon interaction histories. It explored three types of test tasks (multiple-choice, true-or-false, and open-ended), with granular rubrics for LLM-as-a-judge evaluation. Results indicate that LLM performance drops significantly as context length grows and preference expression becomes more implicit, and that generalizing user preference understanding to unseen scenarios poses further challenges. translated_title: 迈向自然个性化：评估个性化用户-大语言模型交互中的长期偏好遵循能力
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）越来越多地充当个人助理，用户可能会在长期交互中分享个人偏好。然而，如何评估LLM在自然、长期情境下遵循这些偏好的能力仍然缺乏充分研究。本工作提出了RealPref，一个用于评估个性化用户-LLM交互中自然偏好遵循能力的基准。RealPref包含100个合成用户画像、1300条个性化偏好、4种偏好表达类型（从显式到隐式），以及长期交互历史。它探索了三种类型的测试任务（多选题、判断题和开放式问答），并提供了细粒度的评分标准用于LLM-as-a-judge评估。结果表明，随着上下文长度增长和偏好表达变得更加隐式，LLM性能显著下降，而将用户偏好理解泛化到未见过的场景则带来进一步的挑战。
tldr: 提出了RealPref基准，用于评估个性化用户-LLM交互中自然、长期的偏好遵循能力，发现LLM性能随上下文长度增长和偏好表达隐式化而显著下降，且难以将偏好理解泛化到未见场景。
en_tdlr: Proposes RealPref, a benchmark for evaluating natural long-horizon preference-following in personalized user-LLM interactions, revealing that LLM performance degrades significantly with longer contexts and more implicit preference expressions, and struggles to generalize preference understanding to unseen scenarios.
